questions.question: What determines which direction is the 'main axis' in a flex container?
options: It's always horizontal, no matter what
The flex-direction property — row makes it horizontal, column makes it vertical
The order of the HTML elements
The width of the browser window
questions.explanation: flex-direction defines the main axis; every other Flexbox alignment property is interpreted relative to whichever axis that currently is.

questions.question: In a `flex-direction: row` container, what does `align-items: center` do?
options: Centers items along the main (horizontal) axis
Centers items along the cross (vertical) axis
Has no effect in a row layout
Centers the entire container on the page
questions.explanation: align-items operates on the cross axis, which is vertical when the main axis (set by flex-direction: row) is horizontal.

questions.question: In the shorthand `flex: 1 1 0`, what does the first `1` control?
options: flex-grow — how much leftover space this item claims relative to siblings
flex-shrink — how much this item shrinks under pressure
questions.explanation: The shorthand order is flex-grow, flex-shrink, flex-basis — so the first value is flex-grow.

questions.question: What layout does `flex: 0 0 240px` on a sidebar combined with `flex: 1 1 0` on the main content area produce?
options: A fixed-width 240px sidebar, with the main content area expanding to fill all remaining space
The sidebar grows to fill the page
Both elements end up exactly 240px wide
questions.explanation: flex-grow: 0 and flex-shrink: 0 lock the sidebar at its 240px basis, while the main content's flex-grow: 1 lets it absorb all remaining space.
